CollegeRecord.title: CollegeRecord
CollegeRecord.description: Authoritative source record held by the College issuer, and the ONLY source of a CollegeDiploma's claims. oid4vc-college resolves the AUTHENTICATED national id to exactly one record here. The School and University issuers must not read it.

collegeStudentId.title: College student ID
collegeStudentId.description: The College's own identifier, e.g. COL-2022-1194. Issuer-side only; never a credential claim.

learnerId.title: Learner ID
learnerId.description: The Education correlation identifier, e.g. EDU-L-004512. This is the value both verifiers correlate across the three credentials. A different namespace and sequence from nationalId and from every institution's student id, because PRODUCT forbids treating any of them as interchangeable.

nationalId.title: National ID
nationalId.description: Issuer-side lookup only, e.g. NAT-70011234. Matched against the authenticated Keycloak account's nationalId claim to decide whose credential may be issued. NEVER issued as a credential claim and never disclosed to either verifier (REQUIREMENTS §2, §7).

qualification.title: Qualification
qualification.description: Controlled vocabulary for the diploma awarded.

specialization.title: Specialization
specialization.description: Disclosable subject area. Requested by neither policy as a threshold; present so the credential carries more than the rules consume.

completionStatus.title: Completion status
completionStatus.description: Controlled vocabulary. Only COMPLETED satisfies either policy; the others exist so that a genuine, fully verified credential can still produce NOT ELIGIBLE.

completionYear.title: Completion year
completionYear.description: Year of completion. Disclosable; not an eligibility threshold in this iteration.

percentage.title: Percentage
percentage.description: Percentage, 0 through 100, at most two decimal places. Compared against a threshold with integer arithmetic (services/verifier/src/domains/education/percentage.mjs) so that a boundary is exact: 60 must pass a >=60 rule and 59.99 must not, regardless of how the value survives JSON. A value with finer precision than the schema permits is a MALFORMED claim, not a business answer. The Master's rule requires >=60 here; the job rule requires only that the diploma was completed.
